Hi Rishi,

Quick question as we finalize the DPA: our legal team is asking for clarity on a couple of operational points around backups and logs. Specifically:

- When a data-deletion request is made (per DPA), what is your guaranteed maximum time until data is removed from all backup systems (S3 snapshots, offsite replication, incremental archive)?
- Are backups ever stored with a third-party subprocessor (we currently see references to CloudVault in your infra docs)? If yes, can we get the subprocessor name, region, and whether they can access unencrypted backups?
- Logs: we need to know retention by default for request/response logs vs. system logs and whether exceptions (e.g., legal hold) can extend that.

We are trying to confirm a 90-day maximum post-deletion retention for backups in our DPA; is that feasible or do you need carveouts?

Thanks — if easier, we can jump on a quick 30m call later this week.

Hi all — quick summary from Security/Infrastructure. High-level answers below; we can provide more detail (audit logs, diagrams) if GreenCloud needs it for procurement review.

1) Standard retention windows (hosted API):
   - Short-term incremental backups (hot snapshots): 30 days TTL by default
   - Cold snapshots / archived snapshots: 90 days TTL for most customers; can be 180 days for dedicated customers under contract
   - System & access logs: default 180 days
   - Request/response logs (PII-sensitive): default 30 days and redaction applies automatically for managed accounts on request

2) Deletion workflow (how we implement DPA deletions):
   - Step 1: Mark primary data for deletion immediately upon confirmed request (T+0)
   - Step 2: Cascade purge to active caches/KV within 24 hours
   - Step 3: Trigger backup expiry job — scheduled purge occurs in the next backup-cycle window; approximate upper bound is 90 days for cold snapshots unless an exception applies
   - Step 4: Final verification + audit stamp logged once complete

3) Subprocessors / backup copies:
   - We use one managed provider for long-term cold storage (CloudVault) in select regions. CloudVault stores encrypted blobs only; keys are managed by Redwood KMS in the customer’s region unless customer has BYOK enabled.
   - CloudVault staff do NOT have plaintext access — encryption uses envelope encryption; root keys are controlled by Redwood KMS.

4) Exceptions & legal holds:
   - We can put a dataset under hold (preserve) while a legal hold is active; that will suspend the backup purge job for that dataset. Holds must be requested by Legal / CS and are auditable.
   - Holds will be logged and timeboxed; any hold lasting longer than 180 days requires executive/Legal sign-off and will trigger a formal exception review.

5) Operational SLA for purge:
   - For standard hosted customers we can commit to an operational purge window of 90 days post-deletion for cold backups (consistent with many cloud vendors).
   - For customers requiring faster purge (<=30 days), we offer a contract option with a technical remediation plan (additional fee may apply due to restore/retention engineering costs).

Attachments: redacted_security_pack.zip (contains SOC2 summary, subsystem diagrams)

If GreenCloud wants the subprocessor addendum language (we have a template) we can propose DPA text to capture the purge SLA and hold process.

— Kim
Sr. Director, Security & Compliance

Thanks Kim — that helps. A couple follow-ups:

- For CloudVault: can you confirm the physical region(s) they store cold snapshots in for GreenCloud (we are EU-based for this workload and need to ensure no cross-border copies unless permitted by SCCs / DPA clauses).
- On BYOK: if we enable our own KMS keys, will that fully prevent Redwood staff from decrypting backups (i.e., enforce customer-controlled key separation)?
- Regarding the 90-day purge: our legal team is comfortable with 90 days if we have an explicit DPA clause that states backups will be irrecoverable after the purge and that you will provide an audit stamp. Can you/Laura propose wording?

Happy to take a quick 20m call to finalize language.

Best — Maria

Hi Maria — I reviewed your draft and added redlines focusing on: purge SLA, subprocessor disclosure, BYOK effects, and audit evidence. Key proposals below (summary):

- Add clause: "Provider will ensure that any cold snapshot or backup containing Customer Personal Data will be deleted from all backup repositories and rendered irrecoverable within 90 days following the Customer's confirmed deletion request, subject to lawful holds."
- Subprocessor addendum: include CloudVault (EU: eu-central-1) and a requirement for Provider to notify Customer of any new backup subprocessors 60 days in advance.
- BYOK: add language that if Customer uses BYOK, Provider will not be able to decrypt backup blobs without Customer key escrow approval; Provider will preserve metadata needed for support but not plaintext payloads.
- Audit evidence: Provider to supply an "audit stamp" (time-stamped log entry and summary report) once purge completes; evidence retained for at least 2 years for auditability.

I attached the redlined DPA for your review. We should be able to accept 90-day purge if the subprocessor location and BYOK language are explicit.

Laura Bennett
